solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Away from head, spots small rash

indicators.note: something taken away from its head has lost its first letter

parts.note: freckles are small brown spots on the skin
S is the usual abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A doctor notices a small rash of spots that is no longer on the patient's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like the medical noun but is the adjective meaning hasty; FRECKLES loses its F before S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash and reckless are synonyms, both describing behaviour careless of danger or consequences.

clue.text: Force into recycling waste

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: recycling something is putting it to use again
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: An instruction to make people sort their rubbish for recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is rubbish, material thrown away as waste.

clue.text: Lily, opera star, missing start of season

indicators.note: missing means a letter has gone, here the one named after it

parts.note: Maria Callas, the celebrated soprano

indicators.note: 'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'season'

parts.note: the first letter of season

explanation.surface: A diva named Lily misses the opening of the opera season.
explanation.definitionFit: The calla is the arum lily, a plant with a large white funnel-shaped spathe.

clue.text: Word for word wickedly retail lie that is banned

indicators.note: wickedly suggests the letters are badly treated and twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: banned means excluded, so those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's wicked lie is reported verbatim, and such lies are forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: LIE without IE leaves L, which joins RETAIL in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal translation follows the original word for word, without interpretation.

clue.text: Hotels seeming to need replacement for exceptional item

indicators.note: needing replacement implies the parts must be put back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hotels apparently need renovation before they can be called outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something else is informal praise for a person or thing that is remarkable or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Small group's endless reason to tour capitals

indicators.note: to tour something is to travel all the way round it, so one piece goes around another
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cause is a reason
UC is short for upper case, i.e. capital letters

explanation.surface: A minority faction is said to have no end of reasons for visiting capital cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' suggests cities, but here it means capital letters, i.e. upper case.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a small, often influential group or faction within a larger political body.

clue.text: Pungent gas in area: more complaining heard

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: moanier means more given to complaining

explanation.surface: A smelly gas in the room makes people grumble more.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'a moanier' matches the gas's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is a colourless gas with a sharp, choking smell.

clue.text: Harassing with knife in competition

parts.note: chiv is slang for a knife
vying is competing

explanation.surface: Bullying an opponent by bringing a blade into a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but the pieces simply run on; being 'in competition' means vying.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivvying is nagging or pestering someone to hurry, a mild form of harassing.

clue.text: Drunken butler then scrubbed with soap

indicators.note: scrubbing rubs things about vigorously, so the letters are thrown around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken butler is cleaned up with soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephano is the drunken butler in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Cloth worker accepting brief hand on return, no job share for him

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a fuller cleans and thickens woollen cloth

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards
something brief is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A textile worker takes on a short-term helper, though he will never share his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' and 'on return' both act on the hand before it goes inside the cloth worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-timer works a whole working week in the post, so he does not split it with a job-sharing partner.

clue.text: One gathering fabric has pain after exercise

indicators.note: after places the second item behind the first in the answer

parts.note: running is a form of exercise
a stitch is a sharp pain in the side, often after running

explanation.surface: Someone collecting cloth gets a pain after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The pain after exercise is the familiar runner's stitch, making the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A running stitch is a simple in-and-out stitch, which when pulled gathers fabric into folds.

clue.text: On tick, passion for silky fabric

parts.note: a tick and a mo are both informal words for a moment
ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: Buying something on credit out of a passion for silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' looks like the British idiom for buying on credit; here 'on' only sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Moire is a silk or similar textile given a watered, rippling finish.

clue.text: Fog is the main worry

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
to fret is to worry

explanation.surface: Fog is the chief concern, as any sailor would say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' reads as 'the chief', but in crosswords it is often the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is the name, especially on England's east coast, for a cold mist rolling in from the sea.

clue.text: Ancient city square very — what?

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
V is the abbreviation for very
eh? is said when asking someone to repeat

explanation.surface: Someone describes an ancient city as very square, then is baffled by the remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineveh was a great city of ancient Assyria, on the Tigris in what is now Iraq.

clue.text: Forgery of Conservative affiliations resolved

indicators.note: something resolved has been broken down and worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political scandal: the Tories' links with others have been faked, now cleared up.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsification is the act of altering documents or records to deceive, which is what forgery is.

clue.text: Pays stooge for somewhere to put a pin up

definitions.text: somewhere to put a pin up

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
a tool is someone used by others, a stooge

explanation.surface: Someone bribes a henchman to find a place to stick a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: A pin is informal for a leg, so a pin goes up on a footstool.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool for resting one's feet and legs on.

clue.text: With dots, marks pages in steps

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: stiles are steps for climbing over a fence
pp is the abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: An editor annotates pages with dots at each stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Stiles are the steps that let walkers climb over a field boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to mark a surface with many small dots, as in drawing or painting.

clue.text: Comprehensive but difficult progress

parts.note: tho is an informal shortening of though, meaning but
rough going describes slow, hard progress

explanation.surface: A sweeping plan, though advancing it is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like a link word but supplies THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughgoing means complete and leaving nothing out, which is what a comprehensive approach is.

clue.text: Love, a requirement to keep you half blind

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within

parts.note: a need is a requirement
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Love is said to keep you half blind, a twist on love being blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone one-eyed sees with only one of their two eyes, so is half blind.

clue.text: Immigrant's earnings resented at first

parts.note: income is what one earns

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of resented

explanation.surface: A newcomer's wages were begrudged by the locals initially.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is someone who has moved into an area from elsewhere, a newcomer or immigrant.

clue.text: Appearance of a magazine with almost half missing

indicators.note: nearly half of the word's letters are dropped from its end

parts.note: taken as written
The Spectator is a British weekly magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine is published with nearly half its pages missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a long-running British political weekly; four of its nine letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect means the look or appearance of something.

clue.text: Dance sequence, old-fashioned, extremely unusual

parts.note: passé means out of date

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of unusual

explanation.surface: A critic describes a dance routine as dated and very odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas seul is a ballet sequence danced by one person, a solo dance sequence.

clue.text: Sensitivity restricting one American historian

indicators.note: restricting something means hemming it in, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: tact is sensitivity in dealing with others
I is the Roman numeral one
US is short for American

explanation.surface: An American historian is so delicate that he holds back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' looks like a description of the historian, but it is a separate piece; the historian was Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian, author of the Annals and the Histories.

clue.text: To which patron contributes a bit?

definitions.text: To which patron contributes a bit?

indicators.note: each word contributes a bit, so the answer is made of pieces of neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A question about what a restaurant customer chips into.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a diner leaves a tip that goes into the shared pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tronc is a pool of tips in a restaurant shared out among staff, to which customers contribute.

clue.text: Somewhat crazy circular

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a little mad, informally
second meaning: full of loops, curving round

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of a slightly odd leaflet; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for mildly eccentric and also literally describes something formed of loops or rings.

clue.text: Old-time reel regularly done spontaneously

parts.note: ex means former
tempo is musical time

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, here every other one

parts.note: the first and third letters of reel

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned Scottish reel performed off the cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-time' looks like a single adjective but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore describes a speech or performance given without preparation, i.e. improvised on the spot.

clue.text: Three-dimensional figure one slashes

parts.note: a solid is a geometric figure with three dimensions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson in which a single solid shape cuts through others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slashes' looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A solidus is the oblique stroke /, and its plural is solidi, from the Latin.

clue.text: Bob, say, means to save time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bob is an example of a cropped hairstyle
second meaning: a quicker route or method

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; here it is a haircut, with 'say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a cropped hairstyle, and the same phrase means a quicker way that saves time.
